key_insight: UNSM changed the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample-dependent way, with detonation-sprayed samples showing 820–970 HV and HVOF samples spanning a much wider 546–1165 HV range.
engineering_relevance: The study indicates that post-spray surface modification can significantly alter near-surface mechanical performance of wear-resistant coatings, but process settings must be tuned separately for each deposition route.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed (DS) and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings after ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM).
Tested four treated samples per route at 20/30 N static load and 20/30 µm vibration amplitude.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN load with 10 s dwell and inspected scratch-induced surfaces by SEM.
evidence_signal: Hardness values and post-scratch SEM observations were reported for the treated coatings, with the highest hardness seen in DS-T1 at 20 N/20 µm and HVOF-T4 at 30 N/30 µm.
watch_item: Scratch SEM images show qualitative damage features, but the abstract does not establish a causal ranking of scratch resistance or separate UNSM effects from pre-existing coating differences.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
